h1: Phakawan Hotel Maha Sarakham — a quiet hotel in a garden that won't break the budget
intro: If you're driving into Maha Sarakham and want somewhere easy to park, quiet, affordable and not cramped like the in-town options, Phakawan Hotel in Waeng Nang is a name that keeps coming up. It's a 20-room, 3-star hotel set in a leafy garden, with an on-site restaurant and free parking. Rooms start from around ฿490/night — the trade-off being a location a fair way out of the town centre.

body.html: Phakawan Hotel sits in Waeng Nang, on the outskirts of Maha Sarakham town — a small 20-room property set in a garden rather than a tall block in the market district. The thing guests mention most is the quiet: no street noise, and free parking right outside the rooms, which makes it a sensible fit for anyone arriving by car.

There are three main room types: a Standard double, a Deluxe Double and a Deluxe Twin. Several guests note the rooms feel more spacious than the price suggests, with a balcony, flat-screen TV, fridge, bottled water, tea and coffee, and air conditioning. Bathrooms are simple wet-and-dry setups — nothing fancy, but fine for a night or two.
"The room is very cute, lovely staff, nice and quiet — for the price it's really good value." — from a real guest review

On breakfast, don't expect a big buffet. It's a simple set — rice soup, toast, coffee, tea, fruit and a few biscuits. Some guests find it fair for the price; others wish there was more choice. If you want a proper meal, it's easier to drive into town and eat at a market stall.

The location needs spelling out clearly. Waeng Nang is outside the centre, a fair distance from the main market and the university area — without your own vehicle you'll be relying on a motorbike taxi or a regular taxi most times you go out. Kaeng Loeng Chan reservoir is about 5 km away and the Maha Sarakham model railway museum roughly 3 km. It suits self-drivers who don't plan to wander the town centre every evening.

To be straight about it, Phakawan isn't a brand-new hotel. Some reviews mention rooms that look dated and could use an upgrade, and a few guests hit patchy Wi-Fi, an unreliable TV or air-con, and a shower that drained poorly. There has also been a report of arriving on a paid booking and being told the hotel was full — so it's worth calling ahead to confirm your reservation for peace of mind.

In short, Phakawan Hotel is a budget stay that does its job well within its price bracket — quiet, with parking, decently sized rooms and friendly staff. It's a good fit for self-drivers passing through, business travellers working in the province, or parents dropping a student at the university who just want a peaceful bed. If you'd rather be in the centre, within walking distance of the market, look at the in-town options instead.

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — Phakawan Hotel Maha Sarakham

faq.q: Where is Phakawan Hotel in Maha Sarakham?
faq.a: Phakawan Hotel is at 349 Moo 12, Waeng Nang, Mueang Maha Sarakham — an area outside the town centre, about 6 km from the central market and Sermthai Complex. It's near Kaeng Loeng Chan reservoir and the model railway museum, and is best suited to self-drivers.

faq.q: How much does Phakawan Hotel cost, and what rooms are there?
faq.a: Rates start from around ฿490/night for a Standard double. There are also Deluxe Double and Deluxe Twin (two single beds) rooms at slightly higher prices. Prices vary by date and platform, so compare a few sites before booking.

faq.q: Who is Phakawan Hotel best for?
faq.a: It suits self-drivers, business travellers working in the province, or parents visiting a student at the university who want a quiet, affordable stay with parking. If you want to be central and walk to the market, choose a market-area hotel instead.

faq.q: Can I stay here without my own vehicle?
faq.a: You can, but you'll need a motorbike taxi or taxi almost every time you head out, as the location is out of town with few restaurants nearby. If you're relying on public transport, a central market-area stay is more convenient.

Yes to both. Breakfast is a simple set — rice soup, toast, coffee, tea and fruit. Wi-Fi is free in all rooms and parking is free. A few reviews mention patchy Wi-Fi or air-con in some rooms, so tell staff if you hit a problem.
